FireSync is a satellite-based wildfire monitoring and data harmonization platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the challenge of combining MODIS and VIIRS active fire observations, which differ in spatial resolution, sensor characteristics, and observation footprints.

FireSync uses spatial and temporal matching to identify relationships between satellite detections, including one-to-many matching that connects multiple VIIRS observations to a MODIS footprint. It also implements Near Real-Time to Standard Processing deduplication to reduce duplicate records. An interactive dashboard provides hotspot maps, 3D Earth visualization, satellite imagery, filtering, fire analysis, and CSV and GeoJSON exports. Its historical burning activity calendar allows users to explore available observations across dates.

By bringing different satellite fire datasets into a unified platform, FireSync aims to make wildfire information easier to explore and analyze. It also clearly identifies unavailable historical periods rather than presenting missing data as zero fire activity.
details:
FireSync: Harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS Hotspots for Historical Wildfire Monitoring

FireSync is a satellite-based wildfire monitoring and analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the challenge of combining active-fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments, which have different spatial resolutions and observation characteristics.

MODIS provides fire observations at approximately 1 km resolution at nadir, while VIIRS provides observations at approximately 375 m. A direct one-to-one comparison can miss relationships between detections or create misleading associations.

FireSync processes NASA FIRMS observations, transforms coordinates into the Equal Earth projection (EPSG:8857), and uses spatial and temporal proximity to identify candidate cross-sensor co-detections. Its harmonization workflow supports one-to-many candidate matching, distinguishing matched clusters from MODIS-only and VIIRS-only observations.

The platform includes an interactive fire map, satellite imagery views, a 3D Earth visualization, observation filters, CSV and GeoJSON exports, and a historical burning activity calendar. Users can explore observations by region, sensor, and date.

FireSync also communicates data limitations transparently. Its current database contains 7,116 recorded observations, but historical coverage is partial. It does not present incomplete data as a continuous historical archive or calculate climatological anomalies without a sufficient baseline.

The project uses React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Leaflet, and Three.js, alongside NASA FIRMS and satellite imagery resources.

Our goal is to make multi-sensor fire observations easier to explore, compare, and understand, supporting more informed wildfire monitoring and research.
